title: SG-2.1 · Merge duplicate content loader/validator into one module
summary: Merge src/content/loader.ts and src/content/world.ts into a single loader and validator, update every import, and cover unknown scene, object, character and flag references in tests.
description: Context: backend/game/src/content has two overlapping implementations of loadWorld and validateWorld. loader.ts returns scenes as an array and validates a LoadedWorld. world.ts returns scenes as a record and validates (WorldDef, SceneDef[]). It does field checks on load. tests/content.test.ts imports loader.ts and tests/validator.test.ts imports world.ts. Desired behavior: one module survives, all imports point to it, and the validator tests cover the surviving one. Expected result: no duplicate implementation remains and unknown scene, object, character and flag references are tested. Why: two diverging validators make content errors unreliable for the later AI development worker.
acceptance_criteria: Given the repo after the change, when src/content is listed, then only one module exports loadWorld and validateWorld and src/content/world.ts no longer exists
Given every file under backend/game/src and backend/game/tests, when imports are searched, then none reference content/world

Given a world whose scene uses an unknown goto_scene target, say character, set_flag flag and discover object, when validateWorld runs, then it returns unknown scene, unknown character, unknown flag and unknown object errors
Given the real the-boys-room content, when loadWorld and validateWorld run, then validateWorld returns an empty array

preserve: LoadedWorld.scenes remains an array of SceneDef
existing error message formats such as 'unknown scene: X'

technical_constraints: TypeScript with vitest and the yaml package; no new dependencies
definition_of_done: npm test and npm run typecheck pass in backend/game
